2607.17668.title: Selectivity Matters: Source Node Influence Pruning for Unsupervised Graph Domain Adaptation
2607.17668.paper_summary: Unsupervised Graph Domain Adaptation (UGDA) aims to facilitate knowledge transfer from a labeled source graph to an unlabeled target graph by mitigating cross-domain distribution shifts. Existing methods primarily focus on node-level feature alignment in latent spaces, relying on the implicit assumption that all source nodes contribute positively to the alignment. However, this assumption often fails because a node's semantic information is intrinsically coupled with its topological graph structure. Due to structural shifts, source nodes with severe structural deviations (e.g., structural outliers) lack semantic counterparts in the target graph, and forcing alignment on them introduces severe noise and causes negative transfer. To bridge this gap, we argue that selective source node utilization is superior to full-graph training, thereby shifting the research paradigm from feature-level alignment to data-level refinement. To this end, we propose Source Node Influence Pruning (SNIP), a novel model-agnostic, data-centric refinement framework. Specifically, SNIP quantifies the structural discrepancy between individual source nodes and the target domain by integrating multiple centrality measures, assigning each source node an influence score. A rank-based normalization mechanism is further employed to eliminate scale variations across different measures, allowing SNIP to effectively identify and filter out structurally incompatible nodes with low influence scores. As a plug-and-play method, SNIP constructs a refined "sub-source" graph that is inherently more beneficial for subsequent alignment. Comprehensive experiments across eight transfer scenarios on five real-world datasets demonstrate that SNIP consistently outperforms competitive baselines and significantly enhances adaptation performance, validating the superiority of selective node utilization over full-graph training.
2607.17668.paper_summary_zh: 無監督圖形領域適應（UGDA）旨在通過減少跨領域分佈的變化，促進從標記源圖到未標記目標圖的知識轉移。現有方法主要集中於潛在空間中的節點級特徵對齊，依賴於所有源節點對對齊的正面貢獻的隱含假設。然而，這一假設往往失效，因為節點的語義信息本質上與其拓撲圖結構相互耦合。由於結構變化，具有嚴重結構偏差的源節點（例如，結構異常值）在目標圖中缺乏語義對應物，強行對齊會引入嚴重的噪聲並導致負轉移。為了彌補這一差距，我們認為選擇性利用源節點優於全圖訓練，從而將研究範式從特徵級對齊轉向數據級精煉。為此，我們提出了源節點影響修剪（SNIP），這是一個新穎的模型無關、數據中心的精煉框架。具體而言，SNIP通過整合多種中心性度量，量化個別源節點與目標領域之間的結構差異，為每個源節點分配一個影響分數。進一步採用基於排名的正規化機制，以消除不同度量之間的尺度變化，使SNIP能夠有效識別和過濾出結構不兼容且影響分數低的節點。作為一種即插即用的方法，SNIP構建了一個經過精煉的“子源”圖，這對隨後的對齊更具益處。在五個真實世界數據集的八個轉移場景中的全面實驗表明，SNIP始終優於競爭基準，顯著提高了適應性能，驗證了選擇性節點利用相對於全圖訓練的優越性。
